title: P16-D verified read grants — canonical authority for scoped operator/telegram operational-status reads
description: P16-D: the Phase-5 verified-identity seam for scoped chat reads. NEW conversation-read-grant.ts — canonical conversation_read_grant entity (schema pair.os.vnext.conversation-read-grant.v1): grant row binds principal_ref (telegram:<chat>|operator:<id>) to an explicit scope {objective_ids, business_ids, own_footprint} + operator_ref + expires_at + ENABLED→DISABLED|REVOKED terminal lifecycle + grant_digest pin + GRANTED/DISABLED/REVOKED event anchors + dedup-key idempotent mint (same semantics replay, different fail-closed). Mint lanes: admin credential (any declared scope) or operator claim (x-operator-id → operator:<id> — the SAME claim authority vnext owner actions already use; may vouch only its own operator_ref and only scope provable via owner_authority_id/BUSINESS_CREATED — foreign vouching fails closed). operational-query.ts: deps.readGrants? seam — verified = isAdmin || granted scope resolved via scopeForPrincipal (ENABLED+unexpired, strict re-proof skips forged rows — tampered grants can never vouch); scopeForGrants = declared ids + own_footprint-derived scopeForActorRef + binding-chain missions; grant-resolution failure denies + integrity note (fail closed). Read path writes nothing (status() is read-only, expired_pending flag instead of lazy mutation). mission-control-server.ts: /api/conversations/read-grants* POST mint/control + GET status inside adminBoundary (operator lane = MC-token claim canonicalized fail-closed; status visibility scoped — operators see only own grants). Granted principals get scoped sections only — providers/executors stay INSUFFICIENT_AUTHORITY (a grant can never become admin, never write, never mint missions). Ungranted/expired/revoked/forged principals stay UNVERIFIED_IDENTITY — default-deny unchanged. serve-mission-control.mjs wires the canonical service into both seams. Codex-only; no retries/fallback; no second authority.
